overall: AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. The complaint was treated as timely, and the letter was properly noticed, discussed, and voted on in open session at the June 17 and August 13 meetings.

allegations.summary: Commission argued the complaint was untimely under the 30-day filing rule because the letter was sent around September 17; the AG disagreed on receipt timing.
allegations.key_passage: We, therefore, treat this complaint as timely and review its merits.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission sent a letter to historic property owners that it never voted on; the AG found the letter was discussed and voted on in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Despite the complainant’s assertion, the Commission voted to approve the letter during its June 17 meeting and then voted on additional information to be included with the letter during its August 13 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant questioned why the Commission had not met in over two months; the AG explained the Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to meet.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to meet, but rather requires that when a public body does meet, it must comply with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, such as posting notice and maintaining minutes.
